title: Railgun query builder: streamline audit search, pagination & export UX
creator: Marco Rivera
description: Goal: Replace the current ad-hoc audit search and ad-hoc export flows with a single coherent 'Railgun' query builder that supports composable filters, permission-aware result sets (RBAC v2), cursor pagination for large result sets, and secure CSV/NDJSON export jobs. This ticket covers backend pagination/export APIs, frontend query builder UX, saved-query persistence, and operational controls for admins (rate limits, retention-aware exports, redaction toggles). Emphasize field-level redaction, per-organization saved queries, and export encryption via KMS. The work must respect SSO/SAML session scoping and admin controls (who can export).
acceptance_criteria: Composable filter UI supports AND/OR groups, timestamp range, actor, resource, event_type, and custom metadata fields
Search results are permission-filtered using RBAC v2: users only see rows they are allowed to view; admins with export permission can export full result sets
Server supports cursor-based pagination (opaque cursor) that is stable across leader restarts for up to 72 hours
Export endpoint creates asynchronous jobs for large result sets and returns a pre-signed HTTPS URL to download CSV or NDJSON; small exports (<10k rows) return streamed response
Export files are encrypted at rest using customer KMS when running in Private mode, or Redwood-managed KMS for hosted; links expire after configurable TTL
Saved queries can be created, named, shared with teammates or org-wide, and show last-run metadata; permissions obey parent folder and role rules
UI shows estimated row count and warns when query will export >100k rows; admin can opt-in to force-export for compliance reasons
PII/redaction settings: fields flagged for redaction are masked in exports unless user has unredact capability; audit events include redact metadata for downstream processing
All changes are covered by unit/integration tests and a design review is logged in links
Telemetry: create metrics for export job success/failure, average export size, export time, and RBAC denial rates
technical_notes: Backend will add /audit/search endpoint with query DSL that maps to current audit-index schema; implement deterministic cursor tokens (base64) that include shard/version metadata
Use streaming NDJSON for large streamed responses and CSV writer that flushes per N rows to keep memory bounded
Export jobs enqueue into export-service backed by a durable jobs queue (Kubernetes CR + Postgres jobs table) and write to object storage (S3/GCS); generate pre-signed URLs
Permission checks enforced at query layer and again at export job execution time; use RBAC v2 evaluation service to compute visible field set per principal
Redaction performed as a post-query transform stage; maintain redaction rules in config and propagate to export-service; metadata column 'redaction_applied' added to exports
Private deployments: integrate with customer KMS for SSE-C or KMS-wrapped keys; hosted: use Redwood KMS with CMKs per-tenant
Pagination must survive leader failover: persist cursor anchor (timestamp + last_id) and include index snapshot version in token
Index optimization: add sparse sort key and time-based partitioning to speed range queries; consider materialized views for heavy queries
Rate limiting: per-org export concurrency caps with exponential backoff and admin override if role permits
Audit the audit: every export job is itself recorded as an audit event with actor, query_id, exported_row_estimate, and storage_location
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): deploy backend search + cursor pagination behind feature flag to 5% of tenants; UI exposes new builder to internal users only
Phase 2: enable asynchronous export jobs and small-streaming exports for all internal staging tenants; run load tests against synthetic audit data
Phase 3: open saved queries and sharing to all hosted tenants; expose export admin toggles in Console (admins can disable exports)
Phase 4: Private mode KMS integration and enterprise rollout after security review
Rollback: toggle off feature flag and revert to legacy search endpoint; expired pre-signed URLs remain valid but no new exports accepted
qa_testing: Unit tests for query DSL parsing and cursor generation
Integration tests: end-to-end search -> cursor pagination -> export job -> download and validate CSV/NDJSON schema
Access control tests for 5 roles: reader, auditor, operator, admin, super-admin covering field-level redaction
Load test: simulated 1M rows query with export to ensure memory and time bounds; measure throughput and 95th percentile export time
Fuzz tests for malformed cursor tokens and concurrent cursor reads during index rollovers
